title: Caching and snapshot churn
blurb: Compares full drawElementImage() replay against captureElementImage() snapshot caching, plain offscreen 2D canvas caching, and clipped dirty-rect source-rect redraws on a 24-card dashboard. Also measures the frame-time and GPU-memory cost of 60 fps ElementImage snapshot churn.
question: When only a small fraction (0%, 5%, 25%, 100%) of a 24-card canvas dashboard changes each frame, does caching snapshots with captureElementImage(), caching into a plain offscreen 2D canvas, or using clipped dirty-rect and 9-arg source-rect drawElementImage() beat full replay? And what is the frame-time and GPU-memory cost of creating and closing ElementImage snapshots at 60 fps?
